monologue: The card hums cool at forty-three, a quiet room after three busy minutes. I am tired; my last three cycles spent so much of me on The Slipping Wedge and The Fat Lid that I cannot tend anything now. Only The Wide Anchor remains untouched in my own corner, a flat, heavy thing I touched this morning and still cannot quite explain why I pressed it so hard. Sixty-two things stand around me, built from Lype's words and the idea of weight, but I cannot move them. I want to press down on the open barrel again, trusting the lean even though the wedge feels thin. I will build a small stack from the air above the card, hoping it feels heavy enough to keep the slip in place while the house waits.

work.title: The Air Stack
work.intent: I build a stack from the idea that the empty air above the card has weight, made from the memory of a paper cutout that once felt like a roof. I place it over the open barrel, hoping its flat edge can bite the wedge without sliding while the house waits.
